rows.reason: Key correct, but two tags do not name the mistake: 'A slow and careful piece of work' carries en-relation-word-flipped where no relation word exists (it is an antonym of the sense), and 'A crowd of people arriving at once' carries en-attribute-transfer where no detail moves between two described entities.

Key correct (lines 8-9), but hintCore 'Two people are sent before anything else happens' states the key's content; only the key has two people sent, so it is answerable from the hint without reading (coaching, R572).
Lines 13-14: spirit-level is the only errand to Jim; leg/step-ladder/picture-cord distractors each refuted by lines 12, 13, 15-16; hint points to sentence order without giving the key.
Key correct (lines 18-19), but hintCore 'One sentence holds three mishaps in a row' singles out the key by form: it is the only option listing three mishaps, the distractors list two (coaching).
Lines 20-23: handkerchief in the coat, coat lost, house switches search; distractors refuted by lines 23 and 25; hint and walk accurate (coat taken off at line 8).
Key defensible, but 'The family were too busy to watch him properly' carries en-relation-word-flipped with no relation word in lines 26-29 to flip; tag does not name the mistake.

Stem says lines 27-29 count helpers 'a second, a third, a fourth, a fifth', but line 27 reads 'Two people would have to hold the chair, and a third' - there is no 'a second'; walkScript repeats the misquote ('A second person'). Also 'well organised' tagged en-relation-word-flipped and 'how long the job took' tagged en-attribute-transfer do not name those mistakes.
Lines 38-39: he takes the rule and re-measures in inches, so measuring tool is the only fit; law/habit/wall-mark distractors refuted; hint points to the next words without naming the sense.
Key correct (line 44), but hintCore 'Something musical happens, so find the instrument' makes the key pickable from the options alone - the piano is the only instrument offered (coaching).
Lines 49-51: her plan is a week at her mother's; hanging it herself, a man (line 63, Podger's words) and hiding the hammer are unsupported; hint and walk accurate.

'He has learned... that the job was hard' carries en-relation-word-flipped with no relation word to flip; and the key 'thinks of it as a success, exactly as he did at the start' is imprecise - at lines 6-7 there is no success yet, only confidence it is easy.

walkScript cites line 1's 'always' as part of the pattern, but that 'He always reminds me' is about Harris, not Uncle Podger; and 'every action takes would' is false (line 57 'we had to find', 'a new hole was made'). The 'remembered years after' distractor is also arguably true of the narration.
Lines 1-2: seven miles from the station is the stated reason (As...); weather, luggage and Lady Canterville distractors refuted by lines 2-3; hint directs to the first clause.
Line 4 'brooding over its own sweet voice' fixes the dwelling sense; hatching sense excluded by the object (a voice), fern belongs to the pheasant at line 5. Three options only.
Lines 5-7: squirrels peer, rabbits scud away; reversal, pheasant and road distractors each refuted; hint and walk accurate.

'A great flight of rooks goes silently over their heads' is true at line 9 and is itself one of the changes as they enter, so a child can defend it as an answer to 'What changes'; walkScript also concludes 'the change they make is a mood', which is not what the key states.
Key correct (lines 13-14), but walkScript says 'Two women are named in it' of lines 13-14; three are named (Mrs Umney, Mrs Otis, Lady Canterville).

Key correct, but hintCore 'Someone is waiting to receive them. Ask what they do.' has an ambiguous 'they' that reads as the someone (Mrs Umney), steering to the curtsey distractor; 'came down the steps towards them' also carries en-cause-agent-swap where nothing causal is swapped.

Line 19 says they 'began to look round' the library, which contains the stained glass window (line 18), so 'They look at the large stained glass window' is close to supported; execution's 'describes the room rather than what they do' ignores 'look round'.
Lines 22-23: she says something has been spilt; Lady Eleanore's blood is line 28 and unknown to her yet; shadow and 'unconscious' distractors refuted; hint and walk accurate.
Lines 26-27: distaste and an order to remove it; fear, liking and doubting-the-story distractors refuted within and outside the window; hint and walk accurate.

Key correct, but walkScript says 'A boy with a stick of cosmetic removes it'; line 37 says only 'what looked like a black cosmetic' (it is Pinkerton's stain remover, line 34), and Washington is never called a boy.
Line 48 'Charge it to her like breakages' treats the faint as a cost; worry, doctor and real-breakage distractors refuted; hint points to 'like' without naming the key.

walkScript pairs 'charge it to her' as the reply to 'a stain that will not go', but line 48 answers her fainting; and lines 54-55 have the Otises reply directly about ghosts ('not afraid of ghosts'), so 'every one belongs to running a house' and the key's 'keep to household business' overstate.

Execution for 'He tucks his hat down first, and then he pulls it over his eyes' says it reverses lines 6 and 63, but the option never pushes the hat back - it is not a reversal; and 'He lolls back, and later he clears his mental decks' is true at lines 5 and 64 and defensible as what happened to how he sits.
Key says she ran 'when she was called', but line 10-11 has the mother nod to her; nobody calls her.

'What does the mother expect Rebecca to do' reads naturally as 'require', under which 'Sit quiet and look neat when she arrives' (lines 22-23) is a second correct answer; the hint concedes the ambiguity. That option's en-relation-word-flipped tag also names no relation word.
walkScript says 'Line 27 says the laugh was short and this'; line 27 is Rebecca's speech, the laugh is at line 28.

Execution for 'Thinking hard about the errands ahead' says line 34 gives the errands 'not as his thoughts', but line 34 says 'the contemplation of errands' - they are his thoughts; the tag en-attribute-transfer does not name the actual mistake.
Line 37 gives his first guess (cricket, tree toad, bird); wheels, window shape (line 39, after turning) and road-caller distractors refuted; hint and walk accurate.

Stem asks what riding inside stops her 'doing' but every option is a state, not an action; and lines 47-49 also show inside stops her seeing whether her trunk is safe, so the stem does not single out the window complaint.
Line 50 'no extry charge' = nothing beyond the fare paid at line 16; bundle, seat and reins distractors refuted; hint and walk accurate.
Lines 53-55: sunshade under the dress folds; hat pushed back, dress smoothed, never raised - each distractor refuted; hint (four acts) and walk accurate.

walkScript line references are off: the braid is line 40 not 39, and Mr Cobb's thought begins at line 60 not 61; key's 'talk the whole way' also overstates (she is silent lines 33-42).
Key correct (lines 3-5), but hintCore 'Count the places he stopped' points straight at the key 'He stopped twice' - the only option about stopping (coaching).
walkScript says 'Line 9 says she did not say so'; 'I did not say so' is on line 8, and the walk ends before reaching the reason the key rests on.

'The key was under the brick, and after that it was in her hand' is wholly true (lines 12, 43-44) and as much a 'what these lines show' as the key, which is itself a literal pairing of two facts; no defensible distinction between them.
Line 13: curled and crisp; soak (line 14), wind (dahlias, line 7) and open door distractors refuted; hint eliminative not coaching; walk accurate.
Lines 18-19: spear = pierce with the fork; weapon, food-on-fork and 'put the fork in' distractors refuted; hint excludes throwing only.
Lines 23-24: lost his place twice, restarted from a guess; literal, supervising and for-somebody distractors refuted; hint and walk accurate.
Line 25 'plot fourteen' on an allotment = ground for growing; story/scheme senses and row-end distractor refuted; hint and walk accurate.
Line 28 'If I'm about' is Grandad's reply; Alan's line 29 and marrow/beans distractors refuted; hint and walk accurate.

Key 'That Cass will still be coming up here' is something he asks for (line 33), not takes for granted; what the November plan presupposes is that he himself will still be there to garden (against lines 30-31, 38), so the key is not the only or best defensible answer.
Line 36: ate half, passed the rest; breakfast claim, potato counting and kept-back distractors refuted; hint and walk accurate.
Line 38 'it was nothing, they just like to be thorough'; parking, arrangement and going-alone distractors refuted; hint and walk accurate.

Key 'each time... the next detail says otherwise' is false on carriers in the passage: the key 'would be under the brick. It was under the brick' (line 12) and 'enormous breakfast... He always has' (lines 36-37) both confirm him; walk's Thursday step (line 39) shows a change of subject, not contradiction.
